title: Working from Home
description: The good and bad sides of working from home, and some tips for doing it well.
instructions: Read the article about working from home, then choose the best answer for each question.

paragraphs.text: A few years ago, working from home was unusual for most office workers. Today, millions of people spend at least part of their week working from their kitchen table or a spare room. Technology has made this possible, as video calls, shared documents and fast internet allow colleagues to work together from different places. Many companies now offer a mix of office days and home days, which is often called hybrid working.

For many employees, the biggest advantage is that they no longer have to commute every day. This saves both time and money, and it can reduce stress. Parents often find it easier to take their children to school or to be at home when they return. Some people also say they can concentrate better at home because there are fewer interruptions from colleagues.

However, working from home has its drawbacks. Some workers feel lonely because they miss chatting with colleagues over coffee or lunch. Others find it hard to separate work from home life, so they end up checking emails late in the evening. Young employees may also find it more difficult to learn from experienced staff when they rarely see them in person.

Because of these problems, many experts recommend a few simple habits. Having a fixed working area, even a small one, helps the brain switch into work mode. Taking regular breaks and going outside for a short walk can improve both mood and energy. Finally, setting a clear time to finish work each day helps people protect their free time and rest properly.

Companies have mixed feelings about working from home. On the one hand, they can save money by renting smaller offices, and they can hire talented people who live far away. On the other hand, some managers worry that teamwork and creativity suffer when people rarely meet. Unplanned conversations in a corridor or kitchen often lead to new ideas, and these are harder to recreate on a screen. As a result, a number of companies now ask staff to come into the office on certain days each week.

The change has also affected towns and cities. In some city centres, cafes and sandwich shops that depended on office workers have lost customers, especially on Mondays and Fridays. At the same time, some local businesses in quieter neighbourhoods have become busier, because people now buy their lunch and coffee closer to home. Some families have even moved away from expensive cities to smaller towns or the countryside, since they no longer need to travel to the office every day.

It is important to remember, though, that many people cannot work from home at all. Nurses, shop assistants, bus drivers and builders all need to be physically present to do their jobs, and many of them work long shifts at evenings and weekends. For them, the debate about home working may seem far from their own daily lives. In the future, the most successful workplaces will probably be those that offer flexibility where it is possible, while making sure that all employees, wherever they work, feel valued and treated fairly.

questions.text: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why companies want all workers back in the office
How to set up a fast internet connection
The advantages and disadvantages of working from home, with advice for doing it well
The history of video calls
questions.explanation: The article describes the advantages (paragraph 2), the drawbacks (paragraph 3) and gives advice (paragraph 4).

evidence.quote: millions of people spend at least part of their week working from their kitchen table or a spare room
However, working from home has its drawbacks.

questions.text: In paragraph 2, the word "commute" means:
options: work late at night
eat lunch with colleagues
change jobs often
travel regularly between home and work
questions.explanation: Not having to commute saves time and money, so it means the daily journey to and from work.

evidence.quote: they no longer have to commute every day

questions.text: According to paragraph 1, what is hybrid working?
options: A mix of office days and home days
Working only from home
Working two jobs at the same time
Working in different countries
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 defines hybrid working as a mix of office days and home days.

evidence.quote: Many companies now offer a mix of office days and home days, which is often called hybrid working.

questions.text: Why do some people say they concentrate better at home?
options: They have bigger desks.
There are fewer interruptions from colleagues.
They work shorter hours.
Their internet is faster.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 says there are fewer interruptions from colleagues at home.

evidence.quote: there are fewer interruptions from colleagues

questions.text: What can we infer about young employees who work from home?
options: They prefer to work alone.
They usually earn more.
They are better with technology than older staff.
They may develop their skills more slowly.
questions.explanation: If they find it harder to learn from experienced staff, their skills may develop more slowly.

evidence.quote: Young employees may also find it more difficult to learn from experienced staff when they rarely see them in person.

questions.text: Why does the writer mention checking emails late in the evening?
options: To show how hard it can be to separate work from home life
To show that home workers are lazy
To explain how email works
To suggest that evening is the best time to work
questions.explanation: It is an example of work continuing into home time, a drawback of working from home.

evidence.quote: Others find it hard to separate work from home life, so they end up checking emails late in the evening.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT one of the habits recommended in paragraph 4?
options: Having a fixed working area
Taking regular breaks
Working at the weekend to finish tasks
Setting a clear time to finish work
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 recommends a fixed working area, regular breaks and a clear finishing time. Working at the weekend is not mentioned.

evidence.quote: Having a fixed working area, even a small one, helps the brain switch into work mode.
setting a clear time to finish work each day helps people protect their free time and rest properly

questions.text: What does the writer suggest about workers who have no clear finishing time?
options: They are more productive.
They may not get enough rest.
They will be promoted faster.
They feel less lonely.
questions.explanation: A clear finishing time helps people rest properly, so without one they may not rest enough.

evidence.quote: setting a clear time to finish work each day helps people protect their free time and rest properly

options: Cheaper office buildings

New laws about working hours

questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 says video calls, shared documents and fast internet allow colleagues to work together from different places.

evidence.quote: video calls, shared documents and fast internet allow colleagues to work together from different places

rewards
rules
decisions
questions.explanation: The paragraph lists problems such as loneliness and difficulty separating work from home life, which are disadvantages.

evidence.quote: However, working from home has its drawbacks.

Companies see both advantages and disadvantages in working from home.
